# ArtX Jobs & Careers: Join Our World-Class Design and Engineering Studio (2026)

At [ArtX](https://artxdev.tech/), we believe that exceptional software is crafted by small, focused teams of high-caliber engineers and product designers who obsess over craft, speed, and business outcomes. 

We are not a bloated IT body shop. We do not micro-manage, bill hours for idle meetings, or settle for average template work. Over 950+ global projects, ArtX has built a reputation for delivering **award-winning digital products, enterprise web architectures, and high-conversion e-commerce engines**.

If you are a builder who values technical autonomy, clean code, modern stacks (React, TypeScript, Next.js, Gutenberg ACF, Tailwind CSS), and high-impact design systems, **ArtX is where you belong**.

---

## Quick Answer: What Roles Does ArtX Studio Hire For?

> **The Short Answer:** ArtX regularly hires for remote, hybrid, and onsite (Sylhet / Dhaka) positions across four core disciplines:
> 1. **Senior Frontend Engineers:** React, TypeScript, Next.js, TanStack, and Tailwind CSS.
> 2. **UI/UX & Product Designers:** Figma design systems, micro-interactions, mobile UX, and brand identity design.
> 3. **Modern WordPress Engineers:** Bespoke Gutenberg blocks via ACF, headless WPGraphQL, and speed optimization.
> 4. **SEO & Growth Strategists:** Technical audits, GEO/AEO framework execution, and conversion rate optimization (CRO).
> 
> We offer competitive salary bands, flexible remote-first hours, performance bonuses, and continuous learning budgets. Send your GitHub/Figma portfolio directly to **artxstudiocom@gmail.com**.

Review our design standard on our [Work Page](/work) and learn about our engineering philosophy on our [About Us Hub](/why-us).

---

## Current Open Positions at ArtX (2026)

| Position | Experience Level | Core Tech Stack | Work Arrangement |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Senior Frontend Engineer (React/Next.js)** | 3+ Years | React 19, TypeScript, Next.js / TanStack, Tailwind, Edge APIs | Remote / Hybrid (Sylhet/Dhaka) |
| **Product & UI/UX Designer** | 2+ Years | Figma, Design Systems, Wireframing, Webflow/Prototyping | Remote |
| **Full-Stack WordPress Architect** | 2+ Years | PHP 8.3+, ACF Pro, Gutenberg Blocks, WPGraphQL, REST API | Remote / On-Site |
| **Technical SEO & Growth Specialist** | 2+ Years | Google Search Console, Screaming Frog, Schema JSON-LD, GEO | Remote |

---

## Why Build Your Career at ArtX?

### 1. Modern Technology Stacks, Zero Legacy Baggage
We refuse to work on obsolete, frustrating codebases. You will work with cutting-edge tools:
- React 19, TypeScript, TanStack Start/Router, and Vite.
- Tailwind CSS and modern CSS container queries.
- Cloudflare Edge Workers, Supabase, PostgreSQL, and Redis.
- Custom, clean Gutenberg block development without bloated page builders like Elementor.

### 2. Craft-First Engineering Culture
We judge talent by output, architectural cleanliness, and problem-solving prowess—not arbitrary degree certificates. If your GitHub demonstrates clean commits, typed interfaces, and well-structured components, or your Figma displays pristine auto-layouts and design tokens, we want to speak with you.

### 3. Remote-First Flexibility with Real Work-Life Balance
We believe deep work requires uninterrupted time. We operate with minimal synchronous meetings, asynchronous documentation, and flexible hours that let you work when you are most productive.

2. **ইউআই/ইউএক্স ও প্রোডাক্ট ডিজাইনার (UI/UX Designer):** ফিগমা (Figma), ডিজাইন সিস্টেম, রেসপনসিভ ওয়েব লেআউট এবং ইউজার রিসার্চে দক্ষ।
3. **কাস্টম ওয়ার্ডপ্রেস ডেভেলপার (Custom WordPress Engineer):** এসিএফ (ACF Pro), গুটেনবার্গ কাস্টম ব্লক তৈরি এবং স্পিড অপ্টিমাইজেশনে দক্ষ।
4. **টেকনিক্যাল এসইও এক্সপার্ট (Technical SEO Specialist):** অন-পেজ, টেকনিক্যাল অডিট, জিইও (GEO) এবং অ্যান্সার ইঞ্জিন অপ্টিমাইজেশনে অভিজ্ঞ।

### বেতন ও অন্যান্য সুবিধাসমূহ (Salary & Benefits):
- ইন্ডাস্ট্রি স্ট্যান্ডার্ড আকর্ষণীয় বেতন ও প্রজেক্ট পারফরম্যান্স বোনাস।
- রিমোট কাজের সুবিধা ও ফ্লেক্সিবল ওয়ার্কিং আওয়ার।

### কীভাবে আবেদন করবেন? (How to Apply)

At [ArtX](https://artxdev.tech/), our design practice operates on a simple principle: **Form Follows Function, and Function Drives Revenue**.

> **The Short Answer:** A modern digital product and UI/UX design agency delivers:
> 1. **User Research & Journey Mapping:** Deconstructing user pain points and mapping friction-free conversion funnels.
> 2. **Scalable Design Systems:** Building component libraries in Figma with standardized design tokens (typography, color palettes, spacing, accessibility contrast).
> 3. **High-Fidelity Interactive Prototypes:** Clickable, responsive prototypes that allow stakeholder testing before a single line of frontend code is written.

Static screens can feel lifeless. We design subtle, purpose-driven animations (hover states, modal transitions, loading skeletons) that communicate system status without slowing down user tasks.

# E-commerce Product Page SEO in Bangladesh: A Practical Guide

A strong product page should help a shopper decide, help a search engine understand the offer, and give an answer engine a clean passage to retrieve. For an e-commerce business in Bangladesh, that means publishing one clear page for each product or meaningful variant, showing the real BDT price and availability, explaining delivery and returns in plain English or Bangla, and keeping the visible page, structured data, checkout, and product feed consistent.

The goal is not to repeat “buy online Bangladesh” in every paragraph. The goal is to make the product the best answer for a specific shopping question.

## Quick Answer: How Do You Do Product Page SEO in Bangladesh?

> Start with a unique product URL and a descriptive title. Put the product name, use case, key specifications, real price in BDT, current availability, delivery area, return terms, and a clear purchase action in the initial page content. Add original images with descriptive alt text, link to the relevant category and related products, and implement accurate `Product` structured data. Validate it with Google’s Rich Results Test and monitor the relevant Search Console report. Structured data can make a page eligible for richer search experiences, but it cannot guarantee a ranking, rich result, or sale. [1] [2]

For a Bangladesh store, local usefulness matters more than adding a city name to every heading. State where you deliver, how customers can contact you, which language the page uses, whether the displayed price includes the charges you want shoppers to understand, and what happens when an item is out of stock. If your business serves Dhaka and other districts, explain that service area accurately instead of implying a physical showroom that does not exist.

## 1. Match One Product Page to One Shopping Intent

A product page should answer a narrow set of closely related questions. A shopper searching for a “cotton panjabi size L” needs a different page experience from someone comparing “men’s traditional wear Bangladesh” or looking for a category of panjabis.

Use the product page for a purchasable item. Use a category page for a group of products. Use a buying guide for a comparison or educational question. This separation prevents several URLs from competing with one another and gives internal links a clear purpose.

Before writing, record four decisions:

- **Primary intent:** the exact product, model, size, color, or use case the page serves.
- **Audience language:** English, Bangla, or a carefully reviewed bilingual presentation based on the customers for that product.
- **Conversion action:** add to cart, request a quote, call, message, or another action that the business actually supports.
- **Evidence available:** original photos, specifications, warranty terms, stock information, delivery coverage, and verified reviews.

Do not create a thin page for every spelling variation or neighborhood. If two URLs contain the same product with no meaningful difference, choose a canonical URL or use a variant structure that explains the relationship between the parent product and its variants. Google’s merchant listing documentation recommends focusing product markup on an individual product or its variants, rather than placing it only on a general product-listing page. [2]

## 2. Write a Product Title That Identifies the Item

A useful title is specific enough for a person to understand without opening five tabs. A practical pattern is:

`[Product name] + [important differentiator] + [size, model, or intended use]`

For example, “Handloom Cotton Panjabi – Navy Blue, Regular Fit” is more informative than “Best Panjabi in Bangladesh | Cheap Price | Buy Now.” The first describes the item. The second is a string of promotional phrases that does not tell a shopper what they will receive.

Keep the visible H1, page title, product name, and structured-data `name` aligned. Google says title links can be generated from the title element and other headings, and recommends titles that are unique, clear, concise, and accurate. [4] A product title should not promise a discount, certification, material, origin, or feature that the product page cannot prove.

The first paragraph should provide the direct answer to the product query. State what the product is, who it is for, and the key reason to consider it. Then let specifications, images, questions, and policies provide the detail.

## 3. Make the Offer Verifiable Before Markup

Structured data is not a place to hide information. It describes information that users can see on the page. Before adding JSON-LD, make the product template reliable:

- Show the current price and currency in a readable place.
- Show whether the item is in stock, out of stock, on back order, or available for preorder.
- Give each purchasable variant a clear selection method and, when appropriate, a distinct URL.
- Explain delivery coverage, expected handling information, and any material delivery charge without inventing a universal promise.
- Publish the return or exchange conditions that actually apply to the item.
- Identify the seller or brand accurately and include a real contact path.
- Keep the checkout price and product-page price synchronized.

Google Merchant Center’s product specification says the submitted price and availability should match the landing page, checkout, and structured data. It also requires prices to use numeric values and ISO 4217 currency codes in feeds. [5] For a Bangladesh store, use `BDT` in machine-readable fields and make the customer-facing currency equally clear. Do not mark an item `InStock` because a cached template says so when the warehouse or checkout says otherwise.

## 4. Use Product Structured Data Without Fabricating Reviews

Google distinguishes between product snippets and merchant listings. Product snippets can suit pages such as editorial reviews where visitors cannot purchase directly. Merchant listings are for pages where shoppers can buy the product from the merchant. The available properties and eligibility rules differ, so choose the documentation that matches the page’s real purpose. [1]

For a purchasable product, a simplified JSON-LD pattern might look like this:

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Product",
  "name": "Handloom Cotton Panjabi – Navy Blue, Regular Fit",
  "image": [
    "https://example.com/images/panjabi-navy-front.jpg",
    "https://example.com/images/panjabi-navy-detail.jpg"
  ],
  "description": "A navy blue handloom cotton panjabi in regular fit.",
  "sku": "PAN-NAVY-REG",
  "brand": {
    "@type": "Brand",
    "name": "Example Brand"
  },
  "offers": {
    "@type": "Offer",
    "url": "https://example.com/products/handloom-panjabi-navy",
    "price": "2800.00",
    "priceCurrency": "BDT",
    "availability": "https://schema.org/InStock"
  }
}
```

This is a pattern, not data to copy unchanged. Replace every value with the product’s real information. Google’s merchant listing documentation identifies `name`, `image`, and `offers` as required product properties for that experience, while product snippets have their own requirement of a name plus at least one of `review`, `aggregateRating`, or `offers`. [2] [3]

Never invent an `aggregateRating`, review count, SKU, GTIN, brand, or availability state to make markup look complete. Schema.org defines a product as an offered product or service and provides properties such as `brand`, `aggregateRating`, and `offers`; those properties only help when their values describe the visible, real product data. [6]

Put product markup in the initial HTML when your architecture allows it. Google notes that JavaScript-generated product markup can make shopping crawls less frequent or less reliable for fast-changing values such as price and availability. [2] A server-rendered or statically generated product page is therefore a sensible engineering choice, especially when the catalog changes often. JavaScript can still power filters, image galleries, and cart interactions after the core product information is present.

## 5. Optimize Images for Search and Shoppers

Product images often carry more decision-making weight than a long paragraph. Use original, sharp images that show the actual item. Place them near relevant descriptive text and give each meaningful image concise alt text. Google’s SEO Starter Guide recommends high-quality images near relevant text and descriptive alt text so users and search engines can understand the image’s relationship to the page. [4]

A useful image workflow includes:

1. Export appropriately sized images rather than sending a desktop original to every phone.
2. Preserve enough detail for a shopper to inspect material, finish, or important product features.
3. Reserve image dimensions so the product title and purchase controls do not jump while media loads.
4. Use filenames and alt text that describe the item, view, and relevant differentiator.
5. Avoid placing important specifications only inside an image; keep them as selectable text.

“Blue panjabi front view” is useful alt text for an actual front-view image. “Best cheap panjabi Bangladesh buy now” is not a description of the image. Do not use alt text as a second keyword field.

## 6. Design the Page for AEO and GEO as Well as SEO

Answer-oriented systems need clear entities and extractable facts. A product page can support that without writing unnatural copy. Put the product name, category, material, dimensions, compatibility, price, availability, shipping area, and return conditions in labelled text that a person can scan.

A useful structure is:

- Product name and one-sentence answer.
- Price, stock state, and primary action.
- Key specifications and what is included.
- Delivery, payment, and return information.
- Original image gallery with captions or nearby context.
- Verified customer questions and answers.
- Related products and the relevant category link.

This structure also gives an answer engine well-bounded passages to retrieve. It does not make a page eligible for a guaranteed AI citation. The same principle applies to GEO: make the business, product, and evidence easy to identify instead of adding vague “best in Bangladesh” claims.

For language localization, do not create a machine-translated copy of the same page and leave awkward terminology unresolved. If a bilingual page is valuable, keep the product facts synchronized while using natural local wording. An English product name may be familiar to a B2B buyer, while Bangla descriptions may make material, care, or delivery instructions easier for another audience. Choose based on the actual customer and provide a clear language path.

## 7. Connect Products to the Rest of the Site

Internal links help shoppers move from discovery to comparison and purchase. Link the product to its parent category, a relevant buying guide, and a genuinely related product when each link helps the decision. Use descriptive anchor text such as “Bangladesh e-commerce website design” rather than “click here.”

If the store needs a broader technical review, see the [ArtX e-commerce website design service](/services/ecommerce-website-design). For an SEO implementation that covers templates, metadata, and measurement, visit [ArtX SEO services](/services/seo-services). The existing [SEO-ready website guide](/blog/seo-ready-website-bangladesh-guide) explains how page architecture, crawlable HTML, internal links, and structured data fit together.

Avoid linking every product to every other product. A small, meaningful set of relationships is easier to use and easier to maintain. When a product is discontinued, redirect or update it only when a genuinely close replacement exists. Otherwise, explain the status and lead the shopper to the relevant category rather than silently sending them to an unrelated item.

## 8. Validate, Monitor, and Update the Template

Before launch, check the page as a shopper and as a crawler:

- Does the URL return a successful response and show the product without requiring a click to reveal the core facts?
- Is the title unique, and does the H1 match the product being sold?
- Are price, currency, stock, variant, delivery, and return details consistent across page, checkout, feed, and markup?
- Do the image URLs work, and does each important image have appropriate alt text?
- Do canonical and internal links point to the intended product URL?
- Does the structured data pass the Rich Results Test without unsupported values?
- Can a shopper understand the next action on a mobile screen?

After deployment, use Search Console’s product reports where applicable. Google recommends checking structured-data reports after first deployment, after template changes, and periodically while analyzing traffic. [3] Monitor errors and warnings, but also review organic impressions, clicks, product-page engagement, add-to-cart events, and completed purchases in the analytics system the business actually uses. A valid markup report is not the same thing as a profitable store.

Update a product page when stock, price, material, warranty, shipping coverage, or return terms change. If the page no longer represents a real offer, do not leave stale structured data online merely because the URL has accumulated links.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Should every product page target a Bangladesh location keyword?
No. Add Bangladesh, Dhaka, or a district when the product, delivery area, or buyer intent genuinely makes the location useful. A product page should primarily identify the product and offer. Repeating a location in every heading makes the page harder to read and does not substitute for accurate delivery information.

### Do Product structured data and Merchant Center guarantee a rich result or higher ranking?
No. They can make a page eligible for certain search experiences and help Google interpret product information, but Google decides whether and how an enhancement appears. Follow the eligibility requirements, keep the page useful, and treat rankings and rich results as outcomes to measure rather than promises to sell. [1] [2]

### How should a store handle size or color variants?
Represent the relationship between the parent product and its variants clearly. Give each variant a stable selection and inventory state. If variants have distinct URLs, make those URLs resolve to the correct selection and keep their visible facts and structured data synchronized. Review Google’s product variant guidance before choosing between one URL with selections and multiple variant URLs.

### Can I add review stars when a product has no verified reviews?
No. Do not fabricate ratings, review counts, or reviewer identities. Show an empty-review state or invite genuine customer feedback through a lawful, transparent process. Only mark up reviews and aggregate ratings that are real, visible, and about the product represented by the page.

### What should I fix first when product pages receive impressions but few clicks?
Start with search-result alignment. Compare the query with the title, product name, image, price context, and first paragraph. Make the offer clearer without adding hype. Then check whether the product is actually available, whether the snippet is accurate, and whether the page gives a shopper enough information to choose it. Use Search Console and business conversion data together rather than changing keywords blindly.

# E-Commerce Website Development in Bangladesh: Design, Features & Price Guide (2026)

E-commerce in Bangladesh has evolved past casual F-commerce (selling via Facebook inbox messages). With over **80 million internet subscribers**, modern Bangladeshi shoppers expect a seamless, trustworthy online shopping experience:
- A page that loads in under 1.5 seconds on mobile 4G networks.
- A friction-free, single-page checkout where they can complete an order in under 20 seconds.
- Native mobile financial service (MFS) payments via **bKash, Nagad, and Rocket**, or instant Cash-on-Delivery (COD).
- Automated tracking updates via SMS and live courier synchronization.

Yet, hundreds of store owners waste capital on slow, broken WooCommerce templates that suffer from 80%+ cart abandonment rates.

At [ArtX](https://artxdev.tech/), we engineer **high-conversion e-commerce engines** built specifically for the realities of the Bangladesh retail market. This comprehensive guide details e-commerce website development costs, essential features, technology stacks, and proven growth tactics for 2026.

---

## Quick Answer: How Much Does an E-Commerce Website Cost in Bangladesh?

> **The Short Answer:** In 2026, the price of developing an e-commerce website in Bangladesh ranges from **৳20,000 to ৳120,000+ BDT** depending on platform and customization:
> 
> - **Starter WooCommerce Store (Small Boutique):** ৳20,000 – ৳35,000 BDT.
> - **Advanced High-Volume WooCommerce Store (With bKash/Nagad & Courier APIs):** ৳40,000 – ৳65,000 BDT.
> - **Custom React / Next.js Headless E-Commerce (Enterprise Grade):** ৳80,000 – ৳150,000+ BDT.
> 
> Essential features must include: 1-click checkout, automated Courier API (Pathao / Steadfast), SMS OTP order verification, and Facebook Conversions API (CAPI).

Explore our live e-commerce builds on our [Work Page](/work) and view detailed package inclusions on our [Pricing Hub](/pricing).

---

## E-Commerce Platforms Compared for the Bangladesh Market

| Platform | Best For | Pros for BD Market | Cons for BD Market | Typical Build Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Custom WooCommerce (ArtX Gutenberg Stack)** | Retail brands, fashion, cosmetics, electronics | Full ownership, zero monthly software fees, native bKash/Nagad/Pathao plugins | Requires solid hosting maintenance | **৳25,000 – ৳65,000 BDT** |
| **Custom React / Next.js Headless** | High-volume enterprises (10,000+ daily orders) | Sub-second speed, zero server crashes during flash sales, impenetrable security | Higher upfront engineering investment | **৳80,000 – ৳150,000+ BDT** |
| **Shopify** | Quick dropshipping & beginners | Rapid 2-day launch, user-friendly dashboard | High monthly dollar fees ($39-$399/mo), costly transaction fees, tricky local MFS | ৳30,000 + $468/yr recurring |
| **Generic Template WordPress** | Lowest budget | Cheap initial price | Extremely slow (6s+ load), high crash rate on sale days | ৳10,000 – ৳15,000 BDT |

---

## 6 Mandatory Features for Every Bangladeshi E-Commerce Store

### 1. Frictionless Single-Page Checkout
Bangladeshi consumers hate long 5-step checkout forms asking for postal codes and multiple addresses. We implement streamlined, single-page checkouts requesting only:
- Full Name
- 11-digit Mobile Phone Number
- Full Delivery Address
- District / Division selection (Dhaka vs Outside Dhaka delivery rates calculated automatically).

### 2. Official bKash, Nagad & Card Gateway Integration
Support both tokenized merchant checkouts and Cash on Delivery (COD). We integrate official APIs from **bKash Merchant Checkout**, **Nagad Payment Gateway**, and multi-gateway aggregators like **SSLCommerz** and **Shurjopay**.

### 3. Automated Courier API Integration (Steadfast & Pathao)
Stop copying and pasting customer names and addresses by hand. With our automated courier integration:
- Clicking "Accept Order" generates a consignment number automatically.
- Delivery labels with barcodes are printed with one click.
- Automated tracking links are dispatched to customers via SMS.

### 4. SMS OTP Verification (Fake Order Protection)
Fake Cash-on-Delivery orders and customer delivery refusal are the biggest profit killers in Bangladesh e-commerce. An automated 4-digit SMS OTP verification at checkout ensures every order is placed with a valid, reachable mobile number, reducing return rates by up to 35%.

### 5. Server-Side Facebook Conversions API (CAPI) & GA4
Due to iOS privacy restrictions and ad-blockers, standard browser tracking misses over 25% of purchase events. We implement server-side tracking, feeding accurate data directly to Meta Ads Manager for laser-targeted retargeting.

### 6. Sub-Second Mobile Performance
Over 90% of your traffic arrives via mobile phones. Our stores achieve **sub-1.5s load times** on mobile devices by compressing media to next-gen WebP formats and caching database queries in Redis.

A standard high-performance WooCommerce store is typically completed within **10 to 14 business days**, while advanced custom headless platforms require **3 to 5 weeks**.

# Is a React Website More Expensive Than WordPress? Real Cost Breakdown & Total Cost of Ownership (2026)

When business leaders, venture founders, and marketing directors evaluate building a new web property, one question inevitably arises during the proposal stage: **"Is a React website more expensive than WordPress?"**

The short answer is **yes, in terms of initial upfront development costs**. Building a custom React (or Next.js) web application requires specialized software engineers writing bespoke TypeScript, state management, and edge-rendered components. Conversely, a basic WordPress site can be assembled rapidly using off-the-shelf themes and pre-built plugins.

However, focusing strictly on day-one invoice pricing is a dangerous executive trap. 

When you factor in **3-year Total Cost of Ownership (TCO)**—including hosting infrastructure, premium plugin subscription renewals, database security breaches, and conversion rate gains—**a React website is frequently far cheaper and exponentially more profitable over a 36-month horizon**.

At [ArtX](https://artxdev.tech/), we engineer both custom WordPress platforms and enterprise React web applications. Here is an honest, transparent financial breakdown.

---

## Quick Answer: Is React More Expensive Than WordPress?

> **The Short Answer:** 
> - **Initial Development Fee:** Yes. A custom React website starts between **৳50,000 to ৳150,000+ BDT** ($500 – $1,500+ USD), whereas a custom WordPress site starts between **৳15,000 to ৳45,000 BDT** ($150 – $450 USD).
> - **Ongoing Maintenance & Hosting:** No. React websites hosted on serverless edge networks (Cloudflare, Vercel) cost **$0 to $20/month** in hosting and require zero recurring plugin renewal fees ($0/yr). High-traffic WordPress sites often require **$50 to $200/month** in heavy database hosting plus **$300 to $800/year** in premium plugin licenses.
> - **The 3-Year Verdict:** For standard content blogs, WordPress is cheaper. For custom portals, high-traffic e-commerce, and high-conversion SaaS brands, React delivers a vastly lower total cost of ownership and higher organic revenue.

Review our transparent package options on our [Pricing Page](/pricing) and examine our client work on our [Work Page](/work).

---

## 3-Year Total Cost of Ownership (TCO): WordPress vs. React

Let us examine the realistic financial investment of running a commercial business website with 50,000 monthly visitors over 3 years:

| Cost Component | Monolithic WordPress Website | Custom React / Next.js Website |
|---|---|---|
| **Upfront Engineering & Design** | ৳30,000 – ৳45,000 BDT ($300 – $450) | ৳65,000 – ৳120,000 BDT ($650 – $1,200) |

# WordPress vs React: Which Is Better for Your Business Website in 2026?

One of the most frequent dilemmas faced by business founders, CTOs, and marketing leaders is: **"Should we build our new website on WordPress or React?"**

Search engines are flooded with queries like **"is wordpress better than react"** and **"wordpress vs react"**. The short reality is that comparing them is fundamentally an apples-to-oranges comparison:
- **WordPress** is a complete, monolithic **Content Management System (CMS)** designed for non-technical users to publish articles, pages, and media without writing code.
- **React** is a powerful **JavaScript component library** (often deployed with frameworks like Next.js or TanStack) engineered to construct complex, lightning-fast user interfaces and web applications.

However, from an executive investment perspective, the question is legitimate: **Which platform will deliver higher conversion rates, superior SEO rankings, and greater long-term return on investment (ROI)?**

At [ArtX](https://artxdev.tech/), we build both custom high-performance WordPress systems and enterprise React web applications. Here is an honest, data-backed architectural breakdown to help you decide.

---

## Quick Answer: Is WordPress Better Than React?

> **The Short Answer:** Neither platform is universally "better"—it depends entirely on your business model:
> 
> - **WordPress is Better When:** You are running a content-heavy publication, a standard business marketing site, or a local service company where non-technical marketing teams need to publish daily blog posts and landing pages without developer intervention.
> - **React is Better When:** You are building a complex SaaS web application, a high-traffic dynamic portal, an interactive custom dashboard, or a brand requiring sub-second page transitions, strict zero-vulnerability security, and tailored component logic.
> - **The Hybrid Winner (Headless WordPress):** Combining WordPress as the backend editorial CMS with React/Next.js as the frontend presentation layer delivers unbeatable speed, top-tier security, and complete editorial ease.

## 4 Core Scenarios: When to Choose Which

2. **You have non-technical internal teams:** If your marketing staff needs to create new landing pages without submitting Jira tickets to developers, WordPress with custom ACF Gutenberg blocks is unmatched.
3. **Budget and launch deadlines are tight:** You need a high-converting, professional marketing website live in under two weeks with minimal capital expenditure.

### Scenario 2: Choose React If...
1. **Your product is an interactive web application:** Portals, SaaS platforms, real-time calculators, client dashboards, and interactive filtering systems are vastly superior in React.
2. **Speed is your primary competitive advantage:** You need sub-second page transitions with zero full-page reloads, providing a native mobile-app feel.
3. **Enterprise security is non-negotiable:** Financial institutions, healthcare providers, and high-profile enterprises cannot risk automated WordPress bot exploits. React decoupled from public databases offers zero front-facing SQL injection attack surface.

# Nagad Payment Gateway Integration in Bangladesh: API Documentation, Charges & Developer Setup (2026)

With over **90 million registered subscribers** across Bangladesh, **Nagad** (the digital financial service of Bangladesh Post Office) has become an indispensable checkout method for modern digital commerce. 

For e-commerce store owners and software developers, integrating the **Nagad Payment Gateway API** offers significant commercial advantages:
- **Lower Merchant Commission:** Nagad offers competitive merchant discount rates (typically 1.2% to 1.5%, compared to 1.5% to 1.85% for competitors).
- **Universal Population Reach:** Extensive adoption across Tier-2 and Tier-3 districts, semi-urban markets, and government stipend recipients.
- **Direct Bank Settlement:** Automated T+1 business day settlements directly into your verified commercial bank account.

However, from an engineering perspective, Nagad's API employs a strict **Public/Private Key RSA Cryptography Architecture** that trips up many junior developers.

At [ArtX](https://artxdev.tech/), our software engineers have integrated secure payment gateways across hundreds of enterprise portals and e-commerce stores. Here is the definitive technical guide to integrating Nagad Payment Gateway in 2026.

---

## Quick Answer: How Do You Integrate Nagad Payment Gateway in Bangladesh?

> **The Short Answer:** Integrating the Nagad Payment Gateway API involves five core steps:
> 1. **Obtain Merchant Credentials:** Apply with your verified Trade License, TIN, NID, and Bank Statement to receive your `Merchant ID`, `PG Public Key`, and `Merchant Private Key`.
> 2. **Generate Cryptographic Payload:** Encrypt request timestamps and order parameters using RSA encryption (SHA-256) with Nagad's Public Key, while signing the payload with your Merchant Private Key.
> 3. **Initialize Transaction:** Send a `POST` request to `https://api.mynagad.com/api/dfs/check-out/initialize/{merchantId}/{orderId}` to retrieve a secure `paymentReferenceId` and checkout redirection URL.
> 4. **Handle Customer Redirect & Callback:** The customer enters their Nagad PIN and OTP on the official Nagad payment page. Nagad redirects back to your callback URL with status parameters.
> 5. **Verify Payment Status:** Execute a server-to-server verification query to confirm funds have been transferred before marking the order as "Processing" or "Completed" in your database.

Explore our e-commerce engineering services on our [Web Development Hub](/services) and review our payment systems on our [Work Page](/work).

---

## Nagad Payment Gateway: Operational & Fee Structure

| Parameter | Nagad Payment Gateway Standard | Notes / Comparison |
|---|---|---|
| **Merchant Commission Rate** | 1.2% – 1.5% | Among the lowest MFS merchant rates in BD |
| **Setup / Onboarding Fee** | ৳0 BDT (Direct Nagad) / ৳5k–৳10k via Aggregators | Direct API application carries no setup fee |
| **Settlement Timeline** | T+1 Business Day (Sunday–Thursday) | Direct BEFTN / NPSB transfer to corporate bank |
| **Security Mechanism** | Asymmetric RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 / SHA-256 | High-grade financial cryptographic validation |
| **Supported Currencies** | BDT (Bangladeshi Taka) | Primary domestic settlement currency |
| **Refund API Support** | Supported via Portal / Automated Refund API | Enables instant customer reversal handling |

---

## Step-by-Step Developer Implementation Guide

### Step 1: RSA Key Generation
Nagad requires OpenSSL key generation:
```bash
# Generate 2048-bit Merchant Private Key
openssl genrsa -out merchant_private_key.pem 2048

# Extract Merchant Public Key to submit to Nagad
openssl rsa -in merchant_private_key.pem -pubout -out merchant_public_key.pem
```
Submit `merchant_public_key.pem` to the Nagad merchant onboarding team. In return, they will provide you with `nagad_pg_public_key.pem` and your unique `merchantId`.

### Step 2: Payment Initialization Payload (Node.js Implementation)
The checkout initialization requires encrypted sensitive fields:

```javascript
import crypto from 'crypto';
import axios from 'axios';

const MERCHANT_ID = process.env.NAGAD_MERCHANT_ID;
const MERCHANT_PRIVATE_KEY = process.env.NAGAD_PRIVATE_KEY;
const NAGAD_PUBLIC_KEY = process.env.NAGAD_PUBLIC_KEY;

// Helper: Encrypt with Nagad Public Key
function encryptWithPublicKey(data) {
  return crypto.publicEncrypt(
    {
      key: NAGAD_PUBLIC_KEY,
      padding: crypto.constants.RSA_PKCS1_PADDING,
    },
    Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(data))
  ).toString('base64');
}

// Helper: Sign with Merchant Private Key
function signWithPrivateKey(data) {
  const sign = crypto.createSign('SHA256');
  sign.update(JSON.stringify(data));
  sign.end();
  return sign.sign(MERCHANT_PRIVATE_KEY, 'base64');
}

export async function initiateNagadPayment(orderId, amount, callbackUrl) {
  const dateTime = new Date().toISOString().replace(/[-:T.Z]/g, '').slice(0, 14);
  
  const sensitiveData = {
    merchantId: MERCHANT_ID,
    datetime: dateTime,
    orderId: orderId,
    challenge: crypto.randomBytes(20).toString('hex')
  };

  const postData = {
    dateTime: dateTime,
    sensitiveData: encryptWithPublicKey(sensitiveData),
    signature: signWithPrivateKey(sensitiveData)
  };

  const response = await axios.post(
    `https://api.mynagad.com/api/dfs/check-out/initialize/${MERCHANT_ID}/${orderId}`,
    postData,
    {
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'X-KM-Api-Version': 'v-0.2.0',
        'X-KM-IP-V4': 'YOUR_SERVER_IP',
        'X-KM-Client-Type': 'PC_WEB'
      }
    }
  );

  return response.data; // Contains paymentReferenceId and redirect URL
}
```

### Step 3: Server-to-Server Verification (Crucial Security Check)
Never mark an order as paid simply because a user returned to your callback URL with `status=success` in the query string. Attackers can forge browser redirects. 

Always execute a backend `GET` request to verify the transaction status:
```bash
GET https://api.mynagad.com/api/dfs/verify/payment/{paymentRefId}
```
Only when the verified JSON response contains `"status": "Success"` should your database update the order state.

content: # Top 7 Technical SEO Tools for JavaScript Websites (React, Next.js, Vue & Angular) in 2026 Modern web development is dominated by JavaScript frameworks: **React, Next.js, Vue, Nuxt, and Angular**. While these frameworks allow engineers to build silky-smooth, app-like experiences, they also introduce complex search engine indexing vulnerabilities. Search crawlers do not process JavaScript like ordinary browsers. Rendering JS requires massive computing power; consequently, search engines like Google use a two-wave indexing system where HTML is parsed first, and JavaScript is deferred into a rendering queue. If your client-side JavaScript throws an unhandled exception, fetches API data asynchronously without proper fallbacks, or takes longer than 5 seconds to execute, **Googlebot indexes an empty shell**. title: Website Accessibility Checklist for Bangladesh Businesses: A Practical WCAG Guide
excerpt: Use this practical WCAG 2.2 checklist to make a Bangladesh business website easier to navigate with keyboards, screen readers, zoom, and mobile devices.
content:
# Website Accessibility Checklist for Bangladesh Businesses: A Practical WCAG Guide

An accessible business website lets people find information, complete forms, and use essential controls with different ways of browsing. Start with semantic HTML, useful text alternatives, keyboard access, visible focus, sufficient contrast, readable layouts, and clear form feedback. Then test the real pages with a keyboard, zoom, mobile devices, and assistive technology instead of treating an automated score as proof that the work is finished.

For a Bangladesh business, accessibility should be part of the website brief from the first wireframe. A customer may read English, Bangla, or both; use a small phone; rely on zoom or a screen reader; or navigate without a mouse. The practical goal is not to add a compliance badge after launch. It is to remove avoidable barriers from the pages people need, such as services, product details, contact forms, checkout, and account areas.

## Quick Answer: What Does an Accessible Business Website Need?

> **The short answer:** Use the [Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) as a technical reference, then build and test for four qualities: content should be perceivable, controls should be operable, instructions should be understandable, and the implementation should work reliably with browsers and assistive technologies. A useful first pass covers headings, language metadata, image alternatives, keyboard focus, contrast, zoom and reflow, captions, labels, error messages, and touch interactions.

WCAG 2.2 organizes testable success criteria around four principles: **Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust**. It defines conformance levels A, AA, and AAA. The levels are not a substitute for user research, but they give a team a shared vocabulary for planning and testing. The W3C also notes that the guidelines do not address every need of every person with a disability, so a quick checklist cannot replace careful evaluation.

## 1. Build a Clear Semantic Structure

Start with HTML that communicates structure before visual styling is applied. Give every page a meaningful title and one clear H1. Use H2 and H3 headings in a logical order, and use lists, buttons, links, navigation landmarks, and form controls for their intended purposes. A heading that is only bold text may look correct while remaining difficult to navigate with a screen reader.

The visual design should also make the page’s purpose obvious. Put the main service or product answer near the beginning, keep navigation consistent, and provide a skip link so keyboard users can move past repeated navigation. For a Dhaka service page, for example, the first content should explain the service, audience, and next action rather than making every visitor search through decorative animation.

Language metadata matters when a site serves English and Bangla audiences. Set the document language accurately, and mark a passage in another language when the language changes. This helps speech tools choose an appropriate pronunciation. Do not assume that displaying Bangla text is enough: check the actual font, line height, wrapping, and contrast on a small screen.

## 2. Give Images and Icons Useful Alternatives

Every informative image needs alternative text that communicates its purpose. A product image can identify the product and the relevant detail; a diagram can summarize the relationship it explains; a linked logo can describe the destination. Decorative images should have an empty `alt=""` so they are not announced as noise. Avoid putting a filename, a keyword list, or the words “image of” in every alternative.

The right question is not “What does the picture look like?” but “What information would a person miss if the picture were unavailable?” The answer may be different in a gallery, a product card, a case-study link, and a purely decorative hero. If text in an image is essential, provide that information as real page text or an equivalent accessible description.

For image links, the alternative should make the destination or action clear. A magnifying-glass icon that opens search needs an accessible name such as “Search,” not an empty label. An icon-only WhatsApp or call control needs text that explains what happens when it is activated. This is useful for screen readers and also makes controls easier to understand when visual assets fail to load.

## 3. Make Every Important Action Keyboard-Usable

Put the mouse aside and complete the main journey with Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, and the arrow keys where appropriate. You should be able to open navigation, reach service links, operate menus, fill forms, submit them, and recover from errors without a mouse. The focus order should follow the page’s meaning, not jump unpredictably through decorative elements.

Do not remove the browser’s focus outline unless you replace it with a stronger, clearly visible focus style. Check focus against dark, light, image, and sticky-header backgrounds. A fixed chat button or mobile navigation bar must not cover the item that currently has focus. WCAG 2.2 includes success criteria for keyboard access, focus visibility, and keeping focused content from being obscured.

Avoid keyboard traps. A modal, carousel, custom dropdown, or embedded payment flow should have a documented way to enter, use, and leave it. Prefer native links, buttons, and form elements before adding custom JavaScript behavior. If a custom component is necessary, test it in the browser and with a screen reader rather than assuming that a click handler makes it accessible.

## 4. Check Contrast, Zoom, and Responsive Reflow

Do not communicate meaning through color alone. A form error should include text and an appropriate programmatic relationship, not only a red border. A selected tab should have a visible state that does not depend on hue alone. Links inside paragraphs should have a recognizable treatment beyond a subtle color change when that is needed to distinguish them.

WCAG 2.2’s contrast criterion sets a minimum ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text, with defined exceptions. Measure the actual text, background, hover, disabled, and focus states. Check placeholder text separately because low-contrast hints can make a form difficult to complete.

Increase text size to 200% and test a narrow viewport. Content should remain readable and usable without forcing two-dimensional scrolling for ordinary text and controls. Responsive cards, pricing sections, tables, and Bangla text need special attention because line wrapping can change the layout. Do not hide the primary action or important instructions when the viewport becomes small.

## 5. Design Forms That Explain, Prevent, and Recover from Errors

Forms are often the most important conversion path on a business website. Give each control a visible, programmatically associated label. State required fields in text, explain expected formats before they are needed, and use clear field names such as “Work email” or “Project budget” instead of relying on placeholder text as the only label.

Error messages should identify the field, describe the problem, and explain how to fix it. “Invalid input” is less useful than “Enter a Bangladesh mobile number in the format accepted by this service, for example 01712345678,” when that format is genuinely required. If a form supports both English and Bangla, make the instructions and errors consistent with the selected language. Preserve valid entries after a failed submission so people do not have to repeat the entire form.

The [W3C forms tutorial](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/) and its [labeling guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/labels/) are useful references for this work. For an ArtX project, accessibility QA belongs alongside the [web development services](/services/web-development) and should cover contact, quote, newsletter, login, and checkout flows—not just the homepage.

## 6. Make Audio, Video, Motion, and Touch Optional

A video that carries information needs captions. Important audio should have a text alternative, and a video may also need described visual information depending on what the viewer must understand. Do not autoplay sound. Give people a visible way to pause, stop, or hide moving content when it distracts from reading or interaction.

Test carousels, animated menus, scroll effects, and 3D scenes with reduced motion preferences and with animation disabled. The core message and action should still work. This is especially important on mobile, where a decorative effect can cover a button or make a form difficult to operate.

For touch interfaces, make controls large enough to activate without accidental taps and leave adequate space between competing actions. WCAG 2.2 includes a minimum target-size criterion with exceptions, so do not turn the number into a universal design shortcut. Check the actual component, its neighboring controls, and the way it behaves with zoom and assistive input.

## 7. Use a Repeatable Accessibility QA Workflow

Run a small review on representative pages before launch:

1. **Keyboard pass:** Navigate from the first focusable element to the final action. Record missing focus, confusing order, traps, and hidden controls.
2. **Visual pass:** Check contrast, text resize, 200% zoom, focus indicators, error states, and reflow on narrow and wide screens.
3. **Content pass:** Review headings, link labels, language attributes, alternative text, captions, instructions, and error messages.
4. **Technology pass:** Use an automated checker to find likely issues, then verify the result manually with a browser and, where available, a screen reader.
5. **User pass:** Include people with different access needs in testing when the website supports a high-value service, account, or transaction.

The W3C [Easy Checks](https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/preliminary/) page is a good first review for page titles, alternative text, headings, contrast, resizing, keyboard focus, and forms. It is explicitly a starting point rather than a complete conformance assessment. Track each issue with the page, component, impact, owner, and retest result. Then include accessibility in the same release checklist as content, analytics, security, and performance.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does an accessible website need to use a specific framework?
No. Accessibility is not exclusive to WordPress, React, Next.js, or another framework. The important questions are whether the rendered interface has meaningful structure, usable controls, correct relationships, and a reliable experience with the browsers and assistive technologies your audience uses. A framework can help or hinder implementation, but it cannot replace testing.

### Is passing an automated accessibility scan enough?
No. Automated tools can identify useful patterns, such as missing alternative text or some contrast problems, but they cannot judge every label, keyboard journey, error message, or whether the text actually communicates the image’s purpose. Combine automated checks with manual keyboard, zoom, content, and assistive-technology review.

### Should a Bangladesh business publish accessibility information in Bangla?
If Bangla is part of the audience’s experience, accessible instructions, labels, errors, and support information should be available in Bangla where the related content is offered. Keep the page language metadata accurate, test Bangla fonts and line wrapping, and avoid presenting a machine-translated interface without editorial review.

### Can accessibility improvements also help SEO and conversion paths?
They can improve clarity and usability, which benefits people trying to understand a page and complete an action. Semantic headings, descriptive links, useful image alternatives, clear labels, and text-based answers also give search systems more interpretable content. Do not present accessibility as a ranking guarantee; measure it as part of a broader quality and user-experience process. See the [ArtX SEO services](/services/seo-services) for the wider technical and content work, and use the [contact page](/contact) to discuss a site-specific audit.

## Sources

- [W3C: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/)
- [W3C WAI: Easy Checks – A First Review of Web Accessibility](https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/preliminary/)
- [W3C WAI: Images Tutorial](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/)
- [W3C WAI: Forms Tutorial](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/)

# Website Migration SEO Checklist: Move a Site Without Losing Search Visibility

A website migration is safest when you treat it as a controlled URL and infrastructure release, not only a redesign. Before launch, map every important old URL to its final destination, prepare server-side permanent redirects, update canonicals and internal links, publish a clean sitemap, and test the new site. After launch, use Google Search Console and server logs to find crawl or indexing problems. This process reduces avoidable disruption, but no migration plan can guarantee a particular ranking, traffic level, or indexing outcome.

For a business serving Bangladesh or Dhaka, the same discipline applies whether the change is a new design, a move from one CMS to another, a new domain, or a new hosting provider. The key decision is whether the user-visible URLs change.

## Quick Answer: How Do You Migrate a Website Without Losing SEO Signals?

> **The short answer:** First classify the migration. If URLs change, create an old-to-new URL map, keep the new information architecture as close as practical, use direct HTTP 301 or 308 redirects, update canonical and hreflang annotations, replace internal links, submit the new sitemap, and use Change of Address only for a domain or subdomain move. If URLs stay the same and only hosting changes, test the new infrastructure, preserve Search Console verification, update DNS, and monitor both servers. In either case, inspect representative URLs before and after launch.

Google’s [site-move guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes) separates URL migrations from hosting changes. It also notes that search visibility can fluctuate temporarily while systems recrawl and reassess the moved pages. A careful checklist is therefore a risk-control method, not a ranking promise.

## 1. Classify the Migration Before Changing Anything

Write down exactly what will change. A redesign can involve several migrations at once, and combining them makes diagnosis harder.

### URL-changing migration

This includes moving from `oldbrand.com` to `newbrand.com`, changing a subdomain, changing folder paths, or replacing URL patterns such as `/services/web-design` with `/solutions/web-design`. Use a mapping between the old and new URLs. Google recommends server-side permanent redirects for this type of move and says the destination should be the final, relevant page.

A domain or subdomain move may also use Search Console’s **Change of Address** tool. It is not a general “tell Google about my redesign” button. Google’s [Change of Address documentation](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9370220?hl=en) says not to use it for an HTTP-to-HTTPS change, a www/non-www choice on the same domain, a path move within the same site, or a hosting/CDN change where URLs remain unchanged.

### Hosting-only migration

If visitors keep the same URLs and you are changing hosting, a CDN, or server infrastructure, follow Google’s [hosting-change guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-no-url-changes). Copy the site to the new environment, test pages and forms, confirm that Googlebot can reach it, preserve ownership verification, update DNS, and monitor the old and new servers. Do not add redirects or Change of Address just because the origin server changed.

### A useful scope rule

Avoid changing the domain, URL structure, content architecture, templates, and language structure in one release unless there is a strong reason. Search Console’s guidance warns that combining a site move with content and URL-structure changes can create traffic loss while Google reassesses individual pages. If the project requires multiple changes, record them separately and keep a rollback plan for each layer.

## 2. Build the Old-to-New URL Map

The URL map is the migration’s source of truth. Export the old site’s indexable URLs from its CMS, sitemap, analytics, server logs, and Search Console reports. Include important service pages, location pages, blog posts, images or downloadable files, and URLs that receive meaningful external links. Do not rely on a short list of pages remembered by the design team.

For each old URL, assign one of four outcomes:

1. **One-to-one redirect:** the old page has a clear new equivalent.
2. **Consolidation redirect:** several genuinely merged pages point to one new page that covers their subject.
3. **Keep and update:** the URL remains valid, so it receives the new content without a redirect.
4. **Retire:** there is no useful replacement. Return the appropriate status and provide a helpful user experience rather than sending visitors to an unrelated page.

Use the final production URL in the map, not a temporary staging hostname. Record the expected status code and destination so a developer or QA reviewer can test it mechanically. For a Dhaka service business, for example, a page about web development should redirect to the new web-development page, not automatically to the homepage merely because both URLs belong to the same company.

## 3. Implement Direct, Relevant Redirects

When a page has permanently moved, use a server-side HTTP **301** or **308** redirect when your hosting environment supports it. Google’s [redirect documentation](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects) explains that permanent redirects are a signal that the new target should be treated as canonical. JavaScript redirects are a fallback, not the preferred migration mechanism.

The safest rule is **old URL → final URL**. Avoid chains such as `old URL → temporary URL → new URL`; they add latency and make troubleshooting harder. Google advises keeping chains low and redirecting directly to the final destination whenever possible.

An abstract server rule looks like this:

```text
/old-services/web-design  →  https://example.com/services/web-design  (301)
/old-blog/seo-guide       →  https://example.com/blog/seo-guide       (301)
```

Do not redirect every retired URL to the homepage. Google warns that irrelevant bulk redirects can confuse users and may be treated as soft 404s. Redirect only when the destination is a genuinely useful replacement or a documented consolidation of the old content.

Before launch, test a representative sample from every URL pattern. After launch, crawl the complete map and record failures such as redirect loops, unexpected 200 responses, 404s, 5xx errors, HTTP-to-HTTPS reversals, or a destination that redirects again.

## 4. Align Canonicals, Internal Links, and Language Signals

Redirects are only one part of the signal set. On the new site, each canonical page should point to its own final absolute URL with a self-referencing `rel="canonical"` where appropriate. Update internal links so they go directly to the new canonical URLs instead of passing through old redirects.

Google’s [canonical URL guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) describes redirects and `rel="canonical"` as strong signals and sitemap inclusion as a weaker signal. The practical lesson is consistency: do not put one URL in the sitemap, a different URL in the canonical tag, and a third URL in most internal links.

If the site has English and Bangla versions, update every `hreflang` reference to the new URLs and ensure each language version has a canonical in the same language when one exists. Check reciprocal annotations rather than changing only the English template. This matters for a bilingual Bangladesh site because a migration can silently leave language links pointing to the retired host or old folder.

Also review links outside the main navigation: breadcrumbs, related articles, XML feeds, structured data, Open Graph URLs, downloadable PDFs, image references, and transactional emails. A page can look correct in a browser while still exposing old URLs in its metadata or content.

## 5. Prepare the Sitemap and Crawl Controls

Create a sitemap containing the new, canonical production URLs. Google explains in its [sitemap documentation](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/sitemaps/overview) that a sitemap can help discovery, especially for a new site with few external links, but it does not guarantee that every listed URL will be crawled or indexed.

Before submission, check that the sitemap does not contain staging URLs, redirecting old URLs, blocked URLs, duplicate variants, or pages marked `noindex`. Keep `<lastmod>` accurate when you use it. Make sure the sitemap is generated from the same content source as the new site so future releases do not reintroduce retired URLs.

Staging protection needs special care. A private staging environment should not be publicly crawlable. If a temporary public hostname is necessary for testing, use the documented noindex approach and remove temporary crawl or index blocks before the production cutover. Re-check `robots.txt`, page-level `noindex`, authentication, firewall rules, and response headers on launch day.

For a useful migration handoff, connect the sitemap to the [ArtX SEO services](/services/seo-services) workflow or your own maintenance checklist, but keep the responsibility with the site owner and development team. Search Console access should remain with the business that owns the domain, not only with an agency account.

## 6. Use Search Console for Pre- and Post-Launch QA

Verify both the old and new properties before a domain move. If you are changing domains, Google requires ownership of both properties for the Change of Address workflow. Submit the tool only after redirects are live and the pre-move checks pass. For a path change or a hosting-only move, use redirects, sitemaps, and monitoring instead of Change of Address.

Use URL Inspection on representative pages before launch and after launch. Google’s [URL Inspection documentation](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9012289?hl=en) distinguishes the indexed result from the live test: the indexed result reflects the most recently indexed version, while the live test fetches the current public page. Inspect the homepage, a high-value service page, a location page if relevant, a blog post, and a page from each major template.

Check the following in each result:

- The old URL returns the intended redirect and ends at the final URL.
- The new URL is reachable without a login or accidental firewall block.
- The HTML contains the expected title, H1, main content, and canonical.
- The new page is not accidentally marked `noindex`.
- The rendered page loads important resources and content.
- The sitemap and internal links use the production URL.

You can request indexing for a small number of corrected or high-priority URLs when the live test is eligible. Treat the request as a crawl request, not an inclusion guarantee. For many changed URLs, a clean sitemap and crawlable internal links are more appropriate than submitting every page manually.

## 7. Monitor the Move After Launch

Keep the old and new properties, redirects, server logs, and measurement setup available during the transition. Review Search Console’s Page indexing and Performance reports for unexpected exclusions, crawl errors, impressions, clicks, and page-level changes. Compare the old and new URL groups rather than looking only at total traffic.

Google says a small or medium site may take a few weeks for most pages to move, while larger sites can take longer. The actual timing depends on the number of URLs and server conditions. A temporary visibility change is not, by itself, proof that the migration failed. Look for specific evidence: redirect errors, blocked crawls, canonical conflicts, missing pages, slow responses, or a sitemap that lists the wrong host.

Keep redirects for as long as practical. Google’s site-move guide says generally at least one year, while the Change of Address help page specifies at least 180 days and longer if traffic is still reaching the old URLs. Updating your own internal links and asking important referring sites to update their links can reduce dependence on redirects over time.

For ongoing [web development services](/services/web-development), document the URL map, release date, status-code tests, Search Console properties, and open issues in the project handoff. A clear record makes the next redesign safer and gives the team evidence for decisions instead of relying on ranking anecdotes.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### Should I use Change of Address for a redesign on the same domain?
No. If the domain and user-visible URLs stay the same, you do not use Change of Address. If individual paths change, map the old paths to relevant new pages and implement direct redirects. If only the hosting provider changes, follow the hosting-migration process and preserve the URLs.

### Can I redirect all old pages to the new homepage?
Usually not. Redirect an old page to the closest useful replacement or to a genuinely consolidated page. Sending unrelated pages to the homepage creates a poor user experience and can be treated as a soft 404. Pages without a relevant replacement should be handled deliberately rather than hidden in a bulk rule.

### How long should I keep migration redirects?
Keep them as long as practical. Google’s site-move guidance generally recommends at least one year, while its Change of Address documentation requires at least 180 days and advises keeping redirects longer when old URLs still receive traffic. Update internal and external links so visitors reach the new URLs directly.

### Does a correct migration guarantee rankings or traffic?
No. A technically correct migration can reduce avoidable problems, but it cannot guarantee a ranking position, traffic level, indexing decision, or AI-search citation. Search visibility may fluctuate while Google discovers, crawls, and reassesses the new URLs. Use Search Console, logs, and page-level QA to diagnose concrete issues.

### What should a Bangladesh business test first after moving its website?
Test the pages that represent real business journeys: the homepage, service pages, contact form, phone or messaging links, location pages, English/Bangla language switches if present, and any payment or booking flow. Then verify that the same pages are crawlable, canonicalized, and linked from the new production site.

## Sources

- [Google Search Central: Site Moves and Migrations](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes)
- [Google Search Central: Redirects and Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects)
- [Google Search Console Help: Change of Address tool](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9370220?hl=en)
- [Google Search Central: Changing your hosting](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-no-url-changes)
- [Google Search Central: Learn about sitemaps](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/sitemaps/overview)
- [Google Search Console Help: URL Inspection tool](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9012289?hl=en)
- [Google Search Central: How to specify a canonical URL](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls)
